scope: Verdict for yoma-002a-s02 only; whole daf (lines 1-39) and Hebrew Rashi read first.

sourceFlowReconstruction.lines1-7: Mishnah: seven days before Yom Kippur the Kohen Gadol is separated from his house to the Parhedrin chamber; another kohen is prepared in his place lest a disqualification befall him. R. Yehudah: another wife is also prepared lest his wife die, from 'vekhiper baado uvead beito', beito = his wife. They said to him: if so, there is no end to the matter.
sourceFlowReconstruction.lines8-14 (s02): Gemara opens 'tnan hatam' (we learned there): seven days before the burning of the parah they would separate (hayu mafrishin) the kohen who burns the parah from his house to the chamber that is 'al penei habirah', north-east (tzafonah mizrachah), and it was called Lishkat Beit HaEven. 'And why was its name called Lishkat Beit HaEven? Because all its acts (kol maaseha) are in dung vessels, stone vessels and earth vessels.' Referents: 'shemah' = the chamber; 'maaseha' = the parah's (Rashi: 'shel parah'). These lines do NOT say: why such vessels were used, anything about impurity/tevul yom/Sadducees (lines 14-20, s03), why north-east (lines 20-24), what Birah is (24-27), any source for the separation or comparison with Yom Kippur (27-38). The words 'mai taama' on line 14 open s03.
sourceFlowReconstruction.rashiOnS02Lines (Hebrew only): Parah = parah adumah; 'al penei habirah' - explained below; tzafonah mizrachah = in the north-east corner of the azarah; 'shekol maaseha' = of the parah; kelei gelalim = cattle dung, explained in Menachot (69b); kelei adamah = not made like earthenware in a kiln but from earth that is like soft stone, from which vessels are carved. Hebrew Rashi on these lines does NOT state that the vessels are not susceptible to impurity (only the English helper text does).
sourceFlowReconstruction.lines14-20: Mai taama: since a tevul yom is fit for the parah (as taught: they would render the burning kohen impure and immerse him, to counter the Sadducees who said it was done by those whose sun had set), the Rabbis instituted dung, stone and earth vessels that do not receive impurity, so that it not be treated lightly.
sourceFlowReconstruction.lines20-24: Why north-east: it is a chatat and a chatat requires north, and it is written 'el nochach penei ohel moed'; the Rabbis instituted a north-east chamber so it have a distinguishing sign.
sourceFlowReconstruction.lines24-27: What is Birah: Rabbah bar bar Chanah in R. Yochanan's name - a place on the Temple Mount named Birah; Reish Lakish - the whole Temple is called Birah, 'habirah asher hakhinoti'.
sourceFlowReconstruction.lines27-39: Mena hanei milei: R. Minyomi bar Chilkiyah / R. Machsiya bar Idi / R. Yochanan: 'kaasher asah bayom hazeh tzivah Hashem laasot lekhaper aleikhem' - laasot = acts of parah, lekhaper = acts of Yom Kippur. Whole verse cannot be parah (lekhaper; parah is not atonement); perhaps whole verse is Yom Kippur? Gezerah shavah tzivah-tzivah with 'zot chukat hatorah': there parah so here parah, here separation so there separation. Line 39 'veeima' begins a challenge continuing on 2b (unresolved on this daf).

boundaryNote: s02 = lines 8-14 (through 'adamah'); line 14 is shared with s03 ('mai taama'). No s02 field draws on the s03 portion.

No field mentions impurity, tevul yom, Sadducees, the reason for the vessels, the reason for north-east, the meaning of Birah, the verse derivation, or a comparison to the Kohen Gadol (items 2, 9 clean). No 'north-east corner of the azarah' (Rashi) is asserted as Gemara (item 6 clean).
Referent: 'all the parah's acts' matches maaseha as Rashi reads it ('shel parah') and as the standard's own item 8 example requires.

Layering: Mishnah content attributed to the cited Mishnah, name explanation to the Gemara, speaker 'Gemara' on both steps (item 6 clean). Order of vessels (dung, stone, earth) matches the page (item 7 clean).
No evaluative labels, no generalization beyond this case, no 'proves/must' language (items 3, 5, 10 clean).
